Definition: from G4862 and the base of G5147; to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively):--break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise.
BiblicalUsage: A bruised reed shall He not break, and smoking flax shall He not quench, till He sends forth judgment unto victory, and the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. In Bethany a woman breaks an alabaster box of very precious ointment and pours it on His head, and a spirit takes a boy, and tears him, and bruises him, and hardly departs from him. The breaking runs through the whole of it: He will not break the bruised reed, He will bruise the serpent, a woman breaks her treasure over Him, and a demon bruises a boy it cannot keep.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the God of peace will bruise Satan under my feet shortly, and I hold that He who will not break a bruised reed is the same One who will crush the serpent. I take the woman's broken box as my pattern: what is broken over Jesus is never wasted.
